newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Meiya expects 1996 net profit to rise 15-20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Meiya expects 1996 net profit to rise 15-20 pct.

text.p: Wool blanket maker Guangdong Meiya Co Ltd expects net profits to grow 15 to 20 percent this year over 1995 due to strong demand for its products, a company spokesman said on Monday.
Meiya expects to produce and sell about six million blankets in 1996, compared with 5.50 million in 1995, the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Meiya's output was 3.8 million blankets in the first nine months of this year, he said, adding that the October-December period is usually a peak season for sales.
Meiya reported after-tax profits of 145.98 million yuan for all 1995, up from 143.77 million a year earlier, under Chinese accounting standards.
Meiya said in an interim report that it had audited net profits of 83.99 million yuan in the first half of 1996, up from 80.77 million in the January-June period of 1995.
About 40 percent of Meiya's blankets were exported to Japan this year, with the rest sold domestically, the spokesman said.

He said Meiya is waiting for final approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission to make a three-for-10 rights offer, tentatively priced at between four to six yuan per rights share. If the issue is approved, Meiya would use the proceeds to expand its blanket production facilities, the official said.
